tier1.text: Each parietal lobe processes touch and the sense of how body parts are positioned. This lobe also receives visual signals about where things are. The parietal lobe sits at the top of the brain. Each half of the cerebral cortex, the brain's folded outer layer, has a parietal lobe.

sentences.text: Each parietal lobe processes touch and the sense of how body parts are positioned.

quotes.quote: Two of the parietal lobe’s main functions are processing somatosensation—touch sensations like pressure, pain, heat, cold—and processing proprioception—the sense of how parts of the body are oriented in space.
quotes.citation: Clark MA, Douglas M, Choi J (2018). Biology 2e. OpenStax.

sentences.text: This lobe also receives visual signals about where things are.

quotes.quote: From the visual cortex, the visual signals travel in two directions. One stream that projects to the parietal lobe, in the side of the brain, carries magnocellular (“where”) information.
quotes.citation: Clark MA, Douglas M, Choi J (2018). Biology 2e. OpenStax.

sentences.text: The parietal lobe sits at the top of the brain.

quotes.quote: The parietal lobe is located at the top of the brain.
quotes.citation: Clark MA, Douglas M, Choi J (2018). Biology 2e. OpenStax.

sentences.text: Each half of the cerebral cortex, the brain's folded outer layer, has a parietal lobe.

quotes.quote: each hemisphere of the mammalian cerebral cortex can be broken down into four functionally and spatially defined lobes: frontal, parietal, temporal, and occipital.
quotes.citation: Clark MA, Douglas M, Choi J (2018). Biology 2e. OpenStax.

quotes.quote: The outermost part of the brain is a thick piece of nervous system tissue called the cerebral cortex, which is folded into hills called gyri (singular: gyrus) and valleys called sulci (singular: sulcus).
quotes.citation: Clark MA, Douglas M, Choi J (2018). Biology 2e. OpenStax.
